title: Bonfire

infobox.Crafting Materials: Surtling core x1, Ancient bark x5, Finewood x5, Corewood x5
infobox.Other Effect(s): Produces smoke, Removes the Cold Effect, Adds the Fire Effect, Rapidly removes the Wet Effect, Reduces Freezing Effect to Cold Effect
infobox.Neutral to (x1): Blunt, ,, Slash, ,, Pierce, ,, Chop, ,, Pickaxe, ,, Lightning

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Bonfires are base structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.
Compared to Campfires, they provide fire over a larger area and do not go out during rain.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bonfires can only be placed on the ground and on stone structures.
• Multiple Cooking stations can be placed around the Bonfire, however, the Cauldron does not work as it needs the fire directly underneath it.
• A Bonfire must be fueled with Wood in order to function. Unlike the Campfire, it requires fueling with Wood immediately after placement in order to burn.
• With 1/10 fuel, a Bonfire will last for roughly 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Bonfire should burn for roughly 13 hours and 53 minutes. This duration is the same for the Campfire.
• Bonfires in captured Fuling Villages can be recycled for their materials, including the Surtling core, if a Workbench is built in their vicinity.
• When exposed to rain without roof or strong wind without 70% cover, the fire gets dimmer and the Fire Effect radius drops from 15 meters to 12 meters.
• Active bonfires create smoke.
• Using a Surtling core or Black core on a bonfire produces a firework-like effect, that is visible to players outside the normal render distance.
• One of the few base structures that is not a priority target for creatures.
